problem: Embodied visual exploration methods (curiosity, novelty, coverage, reconstruction) had each been evaluated on different simulators (SUN360, ModelNet, VizDoom, SUNCG, DeepMind Lab, MP3D), with different architectures, RL algorithms, baselines and metrics. As a result, no two methods could be compared fairly, and it was unclear what works when and why in photorealistic 3D environments.
motivation: Task-agnostic exploration lets a newly deployed robot prepare, without supervision, for unknown downstream tasks such as navigation, localization and reconstruction. Exploration is open-ended and has no single success measure, so it needs a standardized framework and a multi-dimensional evaluation. The authors observe that paradigm rankings flip between small cluttered scenes and large open scenes. They also find that implementation details such as reward sparsity and memory-based features strongly change results.
key_idea: Fix everything except the reward function (same spatio-temporal memory policy, same IL+PPO training, same simulators), then benchmark the four exploration paradigms and several heuristic and oracle baselines. Evaluation uses both visitation metrics (area, objects, landmarks) and downstream-transfer metrics (PointNav SPL, view-localization PSR, concept-reconstruction precision) on AVD and MP3D.
insight: Which paradigm wins depends on environment scale and reward density. In small, cluttered AVD scenes, rewards that prioritize informative views (coverage, reconstruction) win. In large, open MP3D scenes, dense and smoothly decaying rewards (novelty, smooth-coverage) are easier to optimize. The smooth-coverage ablation shows this: adding novelty-style count decay to area-coverage raises area visited from 0.85 to 0.88 on AVD and from 0.54 to 0.58 on MP3D (Table 4). Learned policies are far more robust to sensor noise than geometric frontier exploration (noise robustness coefficient ≈1.0 vs 0.77). Curiosity only learns anything in 3D when its forward model runs on the recurrent memory state: curiosity-cnn with ImageNet features fails completely on MP3D. Imitation pre-training rarely helps; the exception is novelty on MP3D. About 10 training environments already give good performance.
method: Exploration POMDP: RGB-D plus odometer plus bump-sensor observations; discrete actions forward, turn-left, turn-right; finite horizon T_exp (200 on AVD, 500 on MP3D). Each paradigm is just a different reward function.

Standard policy architecture (from Chen et al. 2019): a geometric top-down occupancy map built from depth and pose (height thresholds split cells into obstacle/free/unexplored). Coarse and fine egocentric map crops plus RGB are encoded by three pretrained ResNet-18s (128-D each), fused with learned 32-D previous-action and collision embeddings, fed to a 512-D GRU, then an actor-critic head.
Training: imitation learning on greedy oracle graph-exploration trajectories with ε-perturbation and inflection weighting, then PPO fine-tuning (32/8 parallel actors, 12.8M/8M steps on AVD/MP3D).

Paradigm rewards: curiosity = forward-dynamics prediction error on the GRU hidden state (ICM-style, with normalization practices). Novelty = 1/sqrt(visit count) on a 2D grid (Grid Oracle; 0.3 m cells on AVD, 0.5 m on MP3D). Area-coverage = increment in area seen. New smooth-coverage = mean over seen regions of 1/sqrt(times observed).

New semantic reconstruction reward: K-means (30/50 clusters) on ResNet-50 features of training views defines 'concepts'. A transformer encoder-decoder predicts the J=3 concepts at query poses from the exploration memory. The reward is the reduction in KL divergence to the true concept distribution over Δ_rec steps.

Baselines: random-actions, forward-action, forward-action+, and frontier-exploration (OpenCV contour frontiers + A*). Oracle graph exploration uses the GT connectivity graph to visit random points, landmarks or objects; imitation variants imitate each oracle.

Evaluation: area, object and landmark visitation, each normalized by the best oracle per episode. Downstream transfer: PointNav SPL with an A* planner on the explored map, on hand-picked difficult episodes; view-localization PSR via retrieval, pairwise pose prediction and RANSAC; concept-reconstruction precision@K. Also a noise robustness coefficient (NRC) and a truncated-Gaussian odometry-noise study.

setting.backbone: 3× ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 encoders (RGB + coarse/fine occupancy crops) + 512-D GRU + actor-critic MLPs, trained with imitation learning then PPO (architecture from Chen et al. 2019)
setting.training_data: AVD: 9 training environments. MP3D: 61 training environments. IL uses synthetic oracle graph-exploration trajectories, then PPO RL (12.8M steps AVD, 8M steps MP3D). The reconstruction reward model is trained on oracle trajectories.
setting.action_space: discrete: FORWARD 0.3 m / TURN 30° (AVD graph); FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 10° (MP3D Habitat)
setting.simulator: Active Vision Dataset connectivity-graph simulator; Habitat (Matterport3D)
setting.privileged: Main results use noise-free odometry (effectively GT pose); noisy odometry and GT-vs-estimated occupancy are studied separately. Oracle baselines use the GT navigability graph at test time; learned methods use GT state/objects only at training.

numbers.extra: Own test protocol: 100 episodes sampled from 4 AVD test envs, T_exp=200. Navigation = downstream PointNav SPL (A* on explored map) on 46 hand-picked difficult episodes. Visitation metrics normalized by the oracle. Mean over 3 seeds (±0.02, 0.05, 0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 0.04). Values converted from 0-1 to 0-100.
numbers.evidence: Table 4 'Ablation study on designing a smoother coverage reward function.' AVD row smooth-coverage: 0.88, 0.76, 0.60, 0.41, 0.63, 0.69

numbers.extra: Own test protocol: 342 episodes sampled from 18 MP3D test envs, T_exp=500, Habitat. Navigation = downstream PointNav SPL (A*) on 195 hand-picked difficult episodes. Mean over 3 seeds. Values converted from 0-1 to 0-100.

numbers.extra: Area visited normalized by best oracle per episode. Area_GTocc uses GT simulator occupancy at test time (privileged). NRC kept as a raw ratio.

numbers_note: The main comparison table (Fig. 5, all methods, six metrics, AVD and MP3D, 3 seeds) is embedded in a figure and absent from the extracted text. So are the odometry-noise table (Fig. 6), the dataset-size and environment-size analyses, the curiosity-rnn vs curiosity-cnn ablation, the coverage-variants comparison and the IL-pretraining curves. Only Table 4 (smooth vs area coverage) and the noise-robustness table give numbers. All [0,1] scores (oracle-normalized visitation, PSR, SPL, precision) are rescaled to 0-100 here; NRC is kept as a raw ratio. Benchmarks are the paper's own exploration protocol on AVD and MP3D test environments, not an official task.
results: Paradigm rankings depend on the dataset: on AVD, coverage > reconstruction > novelty > curiosity; on MP3D, novelty > coverage ≥ reconstruction > curiosity. Frontier exploration beats most learned methods on noise-free MP3D but degrades sharply with sensor noise (NRC 0.77 vs about 1.0 for learned methods) and on AVD's noisy depth. The proposed smooth-coverage consistently beats area-coverage (area visited 0.88 vs 0.85 on AVD, 0.58 vs 0.54 on MP3D). The proposed imitation baseline clearly beats the random-actions and forward-action baselines used in prior work. Downstream PointNav gaps between methods are small.
limitations: Simulation only (AVD graph and Habitat MP3D). The architecture is fixed, so architectural advances (e.g. hierarchical or transformer policies) are not studied, and curiosity is limited to 8 parallel actors by compute.
Downstream tasks use fixed hand-designed pipelines (A* planner, retrieval + RANSAC localizer) and hand-picked difficult PointNav episodes. Main results assume noise-free odometry.
All methods need GT depth, pose and state or objects at training time. Main quantitative results are shown mostly in figures.
